questions.q: Find the new profit sharing ratio when a partner is admitted. Use the method 'New Profit Sharing Ratio'. Work with: old_share_fraction = 0.5, surrendered_fraction = 0.45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of new_share.

Calculate the new ratio of all partners after the admission. Use the method 'New Profit Sharing Ratio'. Work with: old_share_fraction = 0.5, surrendered_fraction = 0.2. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of new_share.
Explain in your own words what 'New Profit Sharing Ratio' refers to.
questions.a: Once an incoming partner takes a slice of profit, every old partner's slice shrinks; the full set of revised fractions for all partners together forms the new profit sharing ratio.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'New Profit Sharing Ratio'.
questions.a: Profit shares always total one, so whatever the entrant gains must come out of the existing partners' portions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'New Profit Sharing Ratio', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner

questions.q: Find the old partner's new share under the remaining share method. Use the method 'Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner'. Work with: new_share_fraction = 0.6, old_share_fraction = 0.45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_new_share.

Calculate A's share when C is admitted for a fraction and no sacrifice detail is given. Use the method 'Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner'. Work with: new_share_fraction = 0.5, old_share_fraction = 0.2. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_new_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner' refers to.
questions.a: When the deed is silent about whose shares the entrant buys into, the profit left after the entrant's slice is shared by the old partners in their old proportion; one partner's revised entitlement is his old fraction times that leftover.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner'.
questions.a: Silence about the source of the entrant's share means the old ratio keeps applying to whatever profit remains.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Remaining Share Method for an Old Partner', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: New Share After a Fixed Surrender

questions.q: Find the new share of a partner who surrendered a stated fraction. Use the method 'New Share After a Fixed Surrender'. Work with: old_share_fraction = 0.6, surrendered_fraction = 0.6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_new_share.

Calculate the share left after giving part of it to the new partner. Use the method 'New Share After a Fixed Surrender'. Work with: old_share_fraction = 0.35, surrendered_fraction = 0.2. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_new_share.
Explain in your own words what 'New Share After a Fixed Surrender' refers to.
questions.a: If the admission terms name the exact fraction an existing partner gives up, that partner's revised entitlement is just his old fraction reduced by the surrendered piece.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'New Share After a Fixed Surrender'.
questions.a: Add up every surrendered piece and the total equals the entrant's share.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'New Share After a Fixed Surrender', in plain ASCII form.

How much share has the old partner sacrificed? Use the method 'Sacrifice Share of a Partner'. Work with: new_share_fraction = 0.35, old_share_fraction = 0.6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sacrifice_share.

Calculate the sacrifice made by a partner on admission of a new partner. Use the method 'Sacrifice Share of a Partner'. Work with: new_share_fraction = 0.3, old_share_fraction = 0.3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sacrifice_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Sacrifice Share of a Partner' refers to.
questions.a: For any continuing partner, the piece of profit handed to the entrant equals the share held before admission minus the share held afterwards.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sacrifice Share of a Partner'.
questions.a: A minus result flips the meaning: that partner gained share instead of giving it up.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Sacrifice Share of a Partner', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the sacrificing ratio of the old partners. Use the method 'Sacrificing Ratio'. Work with: sacrifice_of_each_old_partner_in_lowest_terms = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sacrificing_ratio.

Find in what ratio the existing partners sacrificed their profit shares. Use the method 'Sacrificing Ratio'. Work with: sacrifice_of_each_old_partner_in_lowest_terms = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sacrificing_ratio.
Explain in your own words what 'Sacrificing Ratio' refers to.
questions.a: Setting each old partner's sacrifice side by side gives the sacrificing ratio, the proportion in which the goodwill premium is handed over to them.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sacrificing Ratio'.
questions.a: The sacrificing ratio compares how much share each old partner gives up; premium money follows it.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Sacrificing Ratio', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate goodwill at a given number of years purchase of average profits. Use the method 'Goodwill by Average Profits Method'. Work with: profits_total = 50000, years_count = 200, years_purchase = 2600. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.

Find goodwill using the simple average profits method. Use the method 'Goodwill by Average Profits Method'. Work with: profits_total = 120000, years_count = 500, years_purchase = 200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.
Explain in your own words what 'Goodwill by Average Profits Method' refers to.
questions.a: The firm's past profits are averaged over the agreed span, and that average multiplied by the agreed years' purchase is taken as the goodwill.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Goodwill by Average Profits Method'.
questions.a: A steady profit history stands in for the earnings a fresh business would miss in its first years.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Goodwill by Average Profits Method', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate goodwill on the basis of weighted average profits. Use the method 'Goodwill by Weighted Average Profits'. Work with: profit1 = 12000, profit2 = 20000, profit3 = 20000, profit4 = 5000, w1 = 80, w2 = 120, w3 = 120, w4 = 8, years_purchase = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.

Find goodwill using the weighted average with weights one two three four. Use the method 'Goodwill by Weighted Average Profits'. Work with: profit1 = 20000, profit2 = 50000, profit3 = 12000, profit4 = 50000, w1 = 8, w2 = 40, w3 = 500, w4 = 24, years_purchase = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.
Explain in your own words what 'Goodwill by Weighted Average Profits' refers to.
questions.a: Recent years get larger weights, and goodwill is valued by applying the purchase multiplier to the weighted average rather than the plain average.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Goodwill by Weighted Average Profits'.
questions.a: Weights tilt the average toward recent performance when profits show a rising or falling trend.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Goodwill by Weighted Average Profits', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate goodwill by the super profits method. Use the method 'Goodwill by Super Profits Method'. Work with: average_profit = 1500, capital_employed = 2500, normal_rate = 18, years_purchase = 2600. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.

Find the super profit and then the goodwill of the firm. Use the method 'Goodwill by Super Profits Method'. Work with: average_profit = 200, capital_employed = 8000, normal_rate = 8, years_purchase = 200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.
Explain in your own words what 'Goodwill by Super Profits Method' refers to.
questions.a: Only earnings above the normal return on capital employed count: deduct the normal profit from the average profit, then multiply the excess by the agreed years' purchase.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Goodwill by Super Profits Method'.
questions.a: Goodwill exists only where the firm beats the normal rate of return on its capital.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Goodwill by Super Profits Method', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits

questions.q: Calculate goodwill by capitalisation of average profits. Use the method 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits'. Work with: average_profit = 500, net_assets = 50000, normal_rate = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.

Find goodwill as the capitalised value of profits less net assets. Use the method 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits'. Work with: average_profit = 200, net_assets = 50000, normal_rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.
Explain in your own words what 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits' refers to.
questions.a: Capitalise the average profit at the normal rate to get the implied worth of the business, then subtract the actual net assets; the gap is the goodwill.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits'.
questions.a: Goodwill is whatever the capitalized earnings exceed the tangible worth of the business.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Average Profits', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits

questions.q: Calculate goodwill by capitalising the super profits. Use the method 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits'. Work with: average_profit = 1000, capital_employed = 50000, normal_rate = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.

Find goodwill when super profits are capitalized at the normal rate. Use the method 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits'. Work with: average_profit = 200, capital_employed = 1200, normal_rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of goodwill.
Explain in your own words what 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits' refers to.
questions.a: The excess earning itself is capitalized at the normal rate of return, which gives goodwill straight away without valuing the whole business.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits'.
questions.a: This lands on the same figure as capitalising average profits when both start from the same data.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profits', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner

questions.q: Calculate the premium for goodwill brought in by the new partner. Use the method 'Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner'. Work with: firm_goodwill = 3, new_share_fraction = 0.35. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of premium_amount.

How much goodwill premium will the incoming partner pay? Use the method 'Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner'. Work with: firm_goodwill = 500, new_share_fraction = 0.5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of premium_amount.
Explain in your own words what 'Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner' refers to.
questions.a: The entrant compensates the old partners by paying for his own slice of the firm's goodwill; that premium equals the firm goodwill times the profit fraction he acquires.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner'.
questions.a: The premium is then shared by the old partners in their sacrificing ratio.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Premium for Goodwill of the Incoming Partner', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the hidden goodwill of the firm. Use the method 'Hidden Goodwill'. Work with: combined_capital = 8192, incoming_capital = 50000, new_share_fraction = 0.6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of hidden_goodwill.

Find goodwill when its value is not given at the time of admission. Use the method 'Hidden Goodwill'. Work with: combined_capital = 256, incoming_capital = 12000, new_share_fraction = 0.75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of hidden_goodwill.
Explain in your own words what 'Hidden Goodwill' refers to.
questions.a: When goodwill is not quoted, infer it: gross up the entrant's payment to the whole-firm capital, subtract the capital actually standing, and the difference is the hidden goodwill.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Hidden Goodwill'.
questions.a: The unquoted value is read off from how much capital the entrant paid for his fraction.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Hidden Goodwill', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate each old partner's share of the general reserve on admission. Use the method 'Accumulated Profits and Reserves Distribution'. Work with: accumulated_amount = 50000, old_share_fraction = 0.6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_share.

Find the share of reserve transferred to a partner's capital account. Use the method 'Accumulated Profits and Reserves Distribution'. Work with: accumulated_amount = 12000, old_share_fraction = 0.8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Accumulated Profits and Reserves Distribution' refers to.
questions.a: Reserves and undistributed profits earned before admission belong to the old partners alone, so each takes his old-ratio fraction of the accumulated amount.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Accumulated Profits and Reserves Distribution'.
questions.a: The entrant must not benefit from profits earned before he joined the firm.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Accumulated Profits and Reserves Distribution', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the profit or loss on revaluation of assets and liabilities. Use the method 'Revaluation Profit and Its Distribution'. Work with: gains_total = 10, losses_total = 80000, old_share_fraction = 0.4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_share.

Find the net gain on revaluation transferred to the old partners. Use the method 'Revaluation Profit and Its Distribution'. Work with: gains_total = 15, losses_total = 2500, old_share_fraction = 0.2. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of partner_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Revaluation Profit and Its Distribution' refers to.
questions.a: Totalling every upward revision and deducting the downward ones gives the net revaluation result, which the old partners divide in the old ratio.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Revaluation Profit and Its Distribution'.
questions.a: Only old partners absorb revaluation effects, because the assets and liabilities existed before the admission.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Revaluation Profit and Its Distribution', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the new capital of each partner in the profit sharing proportion. Use the method 'Proportionate Capital Adjustment'. Work with: adjusted_capital = 50000, base_capital = 50000, base_share_fraction = 0.2, partner_share_fraction = 0.2. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of capital_adjustment.

Find how much capital a partner must bring in or withdraw after the admission. Use the method 'Proportionate Capital Adjustment'. Work with: adjusted_capital = 500, base_capital = 8000, base_share_fraction = 0.35, partner_share_fraction = 0.45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of capital_adjustment.
Explain in your own words what 'Proportionate Capital Adjustment' refers to.
questions.a: If capitals must sit in the profit ratio, the entrant's payment fixes the whole-firm capital; each partner's required capital is his profit fraction of that total, and the gap against his adjusted capital is brought in or withdrawn.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Proportionate Capital Adjustment'.
questions.a: Capitals are made proportionate to the new profit sharing ratio; a positive gap brings cash in, a negative gap withdraws the excess.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Proportionate Capital Adjustment', in plain ASCII form.

Find which partner gains and which sacrifices when the ratio changes. Use the method 'Share Change on Ratio Revision'. Work with: new_share_fraction = 0.2, old_share_fraction = 0.75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share_change.

Calculate the change in each partner's share after the profit ratio is revised. Use the method 'Share Change on Ratio Revision'. Work with: new_share_fraction = 0.45, old_share_fraction = 0.35. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share_change.
Explain in your own words what 'Share Change on Ratio Revision' refers to.
questions.a: When existing partners reshuffle shares among themselves, each one's gain or loss equals the new fraction minus the old fraction; a negative figure marks a sacrifice.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Share Change on Ratio Revision'.
questions.a: Whoever gains share compensates the one who gives it up, through a goodwill adjustment.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Share Change on Ratio Revision', in plain ASCII form.
